title: Hugging Face Transformers 5.23.0 adds seven model integrations, rewrites the exporter API and lists twelve breaking changes
summary: Transformers v5.23.0 (13 November 2026) adds Inkling 2 Small, LFM3, Dots 3 Note Preview, IQuestCoder and InternLM3, rewrites exporters around ExportedModel, and lists twelve breaking changes. Most breaking entries are titles only, and the notes give no consolidated upgrade checklist.

# Hugging Face Transformers 5.23.0 adds seven model integrations, rewrites the exporter API and lists twelve breaking changes


By OpenTools Team


·


November 18, 2026


Hugging Face Transformers v5.23.0, released 13 November 2026, adds seven model integrations and rebuilds the exporter API. Twelve breaking changes need checking before upgrading.


##


What v5.23.0 is, and what it is not


Hugging Face published Release v5.23.0 of its Transformers library on 13 November 2026, and the release record returned by the GitHub releases API lists it as a normal release rather than a prerelease, carrying the tag` v5.23.0` .[1](https://api.github.com/repos/huggingface/transformers/releases/latest)


This is the open-source Python library for loading, running and training models, not the film franchise — and the date matters: the release landed on 13 November, so it is not a same-day story.


OpenTools has covered this library before, most recently the[Transformers 5.21 MiniCPM-OCR integration](https://opentools.ai/news/transformers-5-21-minicpm-ocr-document-image-pipeline-support) . That article addressed a different minor version and a document-recognition workflow, so it is background rather than a preview of what 5.23.0 changes.


##


Seven model integrations, at different maturity levels


The release notes add seven model integrations:[1](https://api.github.com/repos/huggingface/transformers/releases/latest)


- **Inkling 2 Small** — a multimodal model from Thinking Machines Lab that accepts text and image inputs and generates text. Its language backbone has 48 mixture-of-experts decoder layers, each routing tokens to 8 of 384 experts, for 594B total and 17B active parameters; a Perception Encoder-based vision transformer supplies one embedding per 40x40 pixel patch.
- **LFM3** — Liquid AI's third-generation hybrid model, combining gated short convolutions with grouped-query attention split between full-attention and sliding-window layers.
- **LFM3-VL** — a vision-language family built on LFM3 that takes images and video at native resolution plus text, with a projector merging each 2x2 block of patch features into one language token.
- **Dots 3 Note Preview** — a mixture-of-experts causal language model that accepts native text, image, video and audio inputs, using a shared vision encoder and a Whisper-style audio encoder, with BF16 and FP8 inference supported.
- **IQuestCoder** — code models from IQuest Lab in 7B, 14B and 40B sizes with base, instruct and thinking variants. Its architecture matches Llama, so the auto classes load it through` LlamaModel` and` LlamaForCausalLM` with only` IQuestCoderConfig` specific. The looped` IQuest-Coder-V1-*-Loop-*` checkpoints use a different architecture and are not supported.
- **InternLM3** — an 8B instruction-tuned model from Shanghai AI Laboratory that likewise loads through the Llama implementation, with` InternLM3Config` requiring its` attention_bias` and` mlp_bias` values to be equal, as they are in the released checkpoints.
- **JEV** — a decision head that scores single-token labels with a linear layer at the last token of the prompt, reading head files shipped beside the weights and able to run through the` decision` pipeline or` decide` .


JEV is the one addition the notes explicitly mark as unsettled: they describe it and the` decision` pipeline as currently experimental, say their APIs, configuration and behaviour may change, and warn they should be "used with caution in production environments".[1](https://api.github.com/repos/huggingface/transformers/releases/latest) If you plan to put a decision head into production, that note is the relevant boundary rather than the model's inclusion in the library.


The release notes link documentation pages for each addition, but those pages were not part of the evidence reviewed here, so checkpoint availability, licensing and hardware requirements for the new models are not established by this article.


##


The exporter rewrite is the change most likely to touch deployment tooling


Exporters were rebuilt around a single object. Every export now returns an` ExportedModel` you call the way you call the original model, push to the Hub, and load back on the backend's own runtime, with the same API spanning Dynamo, ONNX Runtime, OpenVINO and ExecuTorch.[1](https://api.github.com/repos/huggingface/transformers/releases/latest) Quantized exports (PT2E, NNCF, ONNX Runtime) save and run the same way.


This is also a breaking API change, and one of the few the notes spell out:` export()` returns an` ExportedModel` , an ONNX program is an` onnx_ir.Model` , the` output_path` options on` OnnxConfig` and` OpenVINOConfig` are gone in favour of` save_pretrained` , and custom backends register with` register_backend` . Any script that passes` output_path` or expects the old return type will need editing.


The notes also carry vendor-stated speedups, which are the project's own figures rather than independent measurements:


- OpenVINO exports now reach OpenVINO's fused CPU kernels, which the notes say makes decode 2.4–3.9x faster than before.
- On EmbeddingGemma2 (8 x 128 tokens), ONNX Runtime with the TensorRT EP is reported 7.6x faster than eager PyTorch and 1.4x faster than` torch.compile` on an A100.
- OpenVINO is reported 4.1x faster than eager and 2.2x faster than` torch.compile` on a Xeon Platinum 8570 (4.9x and 2.6x with int8 weights).


The notes do not state the batch size, precision or baseline version behind the "2.4–3.9x faster than before" comparison, so treat that range as a claim about the exporter path rather than a prediction for your workload.


##


Twelve breaking changes, most stated as titles only


The notes open a dedicated breaking-changes section with twelve entries.[1](https://api.github.com/repos/huggingface/transformers/releases/latest) For most of them the entry is a one-line title, so the notes establish that a change happened without stating what code it breaks or what replaces it.


The entries that come with usable detail are the two audio changes and the exporter rewrite:


- The` \[audio\]` extra is slimmed to torchaudio, soundfile and soxr, dropping librosa and phonemizer — so the new install surface is stated, even if which pipelines break beyond the dependency change is not.
- ` Wav2Vec2ProcessorWithLM` and the pyctcdecode/kenlm language-model decoding path are deprecated, with no removal date given.
- The exporter API break described above.


The remaining entries are titles without stated impact: removing the` ep_router` expert-parallel style, running MXFP4 GPT-OSS experts through` ep_dispatch_experts` , adding a` deepgemm_megamoe` expert-parallel implementation, moving processing defaults to the class, dropping rope deltas from` ModelOutput` , the` kernels` minimum-version bump, an attention change for Mac users in` serve` , "safe-izing" pi0 graphs, and building the tp/ep_plan/fsdp_plan once.


Practically, that means the notes tell you which areas to inspect — expert parallelism, processor defaults, rope deltas, kernels, Mac serving — but not what your own code must change. The linked pull requests are where the detail sits.


##


Inference, loading and training fixes that affect upgrades


Several fixes land on paths that deployments commonly hit:[1](https://api.github.com/repos/huggingface/transformers/releases/latest)


- Cache correctness: Gemma4 static cache attending to empty slots in KV-shared layers at prefill, Qwen VL positions when a text cache is reused with a new image, and DeepSeek-V4 compression cache reordering during beam search.
- Generation: grouped-query attention decoding now folds query heads onto their KV head instead of repeating K and V, which the notes describe as avoiding a copy of the KV cache; padded generation, batched decoding and pipeline metadata each get a fix.
- Loading: mismatched keys are no longer silently ignored.
- Quantization: FP8` modules_to_not_convert` entries are renamed like weight names, so modules such as` f_a_proj` and` f_b_proj` are no longer wrongly quantized, and MXFP4 experts dequantize to the requested dtype instead of always using bfloat16.


For fine-tuning and distributed runs, the notes describe a selectable` ep_implementation` for expert parallelism — all-reduce for CUDA-graph-friendly inference, all-to-all for training — a Trainer change that reduces FSDP/HSDP gradients only on the last micro-batch, and token-count normalization corrected to use true division. The release also raises the minimum` kernels` version and bumps mamba-ssm kernels, and the project's Docker and CI images move to torch 2.15 / cu132. The notes do not say whether torch 2.15 is a user-facing minimum or only the environment the project tests against.


##


What the official notes do not establish


Three limits are worth carrying into an upgrade decision.


First, there is no consolidated migration checklist. The notes list breaking changes, deprecated audio components and the exporter API break, and then point at pull requests; a version-5 migration guide is referenced for one vision note (that` hidden_states\[-1\]` of vision models is pre-norm), but its coverage of the twelve breaking entries is not established here.[1](https://api.github.com/repos/huggingface/transformers/releases/latest)


Second, the notes are not an exhaustive changelog. They support statements of the form "the notes state X", never "X is the only change" — and several section summaries inside the release notes end mid-sentence, so their remaining detail lives in the linked pull requests rather than in the note text.


Third, nothing here replaces a trial. No install, upgrade or fine-tuning run was performed while writing this article, and the dependency floors the notes mention — the` kernels` minimum in particular — are not stated as numbers. Check the specific pull requests for your own expert-parallelism, audio, exporter and quantization paths before treating 5.23.0 as a drop-in replacement.
